dedupe_keys.name: cropforge code first python virtual farm and crop simulation engine

description: CropForge is an open-source Python engine for running virtual farm experiments in code instead of configuration files or graphical tools. Saswat Sundar Rath at ICAR-IARI Jharkhand wrote it for crop scientists; the documentation calls it a code-first virtual farm runtime and shows a wheat example, with weather and soil parameters read from CSV loaders and results written as Parquet logs and shown in a FastAPI and Plotly Dash dashboard with 3D plant rendering. It needs Python 3.12 or later, is MIT licensed and free, and the documentation lists v1.0.0 as release-ready with physics modelling and multi-field dashboards from v0.2.0. Coverage is any farm site with weather and soil data. Caveats: the documentation gives no repository link, no validation against field trials was read, and the list of supported crops is not complete on the page. It suits agent-based and capacity studies of agricultural production and food supply chains, and as a component in linked infrastructure and land use scenarios. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
